device.description: 12-bit 1-channel voltage-output DAC with 2.5-V reference, SPI or I2C interface
device.note: dac60501.pdf (SBAS794E) p.3 pinout (Table 6-1), p.4 recommended operating conditions, p.9-10 timing, p.21-22 DAC register structure, p.23 SPI mode, p.24-28 I2C (Tables 8-1 to 8-5), p.29-32 register map

registers.name: DEVID
registers.note: p.29: 0x2115 for DAC60501Z (zero-scale reset); DAC60501M reads 0x2195 (RSTSEL = 1)

registers.name: TRIGGER
registers.note: p.31: write-only, self-resetting; handled by the TRIGGER commands

registers.name: DAC
registers.note: p.32: DAC data MSB aligned (12 bits in 15:4, low bits don't care); reset 0000h for Z parts, 8000h for M parts

registers.name: DAC_ACT
registers.note: DAC active register (internal, section 8.3.1.2): loaded from DAC at once (asynchronous mode) or by the TRIGGER LDAC bit (synchronous mode)

commands.name: Command byte (NOOP/DEVID/SYNC/CONFIG)
commands.note: p.26-28: Table 8-4 command byte selects the register; the MSDB and LSDB that follow are written to it; a write of only the command byte then a repeated-start read returns that register, MSB first

commands.name: Command byte (TRIGGER)
commands.note: TRIGGER (5h) written through the pointer; SOFT-RESET and LDAC run as protocol.triggers

commands.name: Command byte (DAC DATA)
commands.note: asynchronous mode (SYNC.DAC_SYNC_EN = 0): each register written through the pointer updates the active register at once

commands.name: Command byte (DAC DATA) (synchronous)
commands.note: synchronous mode: the active register updates on the TRIGGER LDAC bit

pages: p.3 (pinout), p.4 (ROC), p.9-10 (I2C timing), p.21-22 (register structure, POR), p.23 (SPI), p.24-28 (I2C, address and command byte), p.29-32 (registers)
notModeled: analog output, internal reference, REF-DIV, gain, power-down and reference alarm (stored only)

SPI mode (SPI2C = 0): a write-only 3-wire SYNC/SCLK/SDIN interface with 24-bit frames (command byte + 16 data bits, latched at SYNC rising, frames shorter than 24 SCLK falling edges discarded); the model is the I2C mode (SPI2C = 1), which has read-back
TRIGGER.LDAC and SOFT-RESET self-clear in the chip; the model leaves the written value in TRIGGER (each later TRIGGER write with LDAC = 1 updates again)
command bytes with B23-B20 non-zero and the undocumented address 6 are ignored
I2C fast-mode plus and the 250-us POR delay
variants: dac60501.pdf covers DAC80501 (16-bit), DAC70501 (14-bit) and DAC60501 (12-bit), each in Z (zero-scale) and M (midscale) power-on versions; own spec files, identical except bits, DEVID and the DAC data alignment
